clue.text: Authorisation for each assignment

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'
a mission is a task or assignment someone is sent to do

explanation.surface: A manager signs off approval for every task handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is the formal granting of leave to act, which is what an authorisation gives.

clue.text: Sherpa's first to leave most demanding mountain

indicators.note: to leave says a letter goes out of the word built from 'most demanding'

parts.note: severest means harshest or most demanding

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word Sherpa's

explanation.surface: A Himalayan guide quits the hardest peak, the first of his team to drop out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes S from Sherpa's and 'to leave' removes it from SEVEREST. Sherpas are the Nepalese people famous as Himalayan guides, which makes the surface fit the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest peak, on the Nepal-Tibet border: a specific example of a mountain.

clue.text: Type score

definitions.meaning: a ... is a brand or type of product, as in 'what ... is your car?'
to score, as in making a run in cricket or making points

explanation.surface: Two bare words that might be typesetting or music jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Make is both a noun for a brand or kind of product and a verb meaning to achieve or score.

clue.text: Army engineer's forged papers

indicators.note: forged means faked or fashioned, so the letters of papers are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A military engineer has been caught with counterfeit documents.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'engineer' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a soldier of the engineering corps, originally one who dug saps, or siege trenches.

clue.text: Attempt to follow long Asian river? That'll be hard work

indicators.note: to follow says the word for an attempt comes after the river in the answer

parts.note: the Indus is a long river flowing through Pakistan
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone planning a journey along a great Asian river is warned it will be exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry can mean diligence or hard-working effort, as in praising someone's industry.

clue.text: Hot in pleasant recess

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for hot sits inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warm, agreeable alcove somewhere in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow recess in a wall, often holding a statue or ornament.

clue.text: Valet in husband's tavern, drunk

parts.note: man is an informal word for a husband, so husband's gives man's

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of tavern are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman's servant is found in his master's pub, intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives ERVANT from the pub; 'husband's' looks like part of the scene but supplies the opening word, and 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a man employed as a personal attendant, the same job as a manservant.

clue.text: Point during drink, and talk louder

indicators.note: during says the word for point comes in the middle of the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
a peak is a pointed top, a point

explanation.surface: Someone sipping a pint is told to raise their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak up is the idiom for raising one's voice so others can hear.

clue.text: Unexpected, small rebellion involving Republican

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: involving means taking something within, so the rebellion word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: an uprising is a rebellion

explanation.surface: A minor revolt in which a Republican takes part catches everyone off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes between the U and P of UPRISING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising is not foreseen, so it is unexpected: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Beginning to drink a tea in Boris's country cottage?

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word drink

parts.note: cha (or char) is informal British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A man called Boris starts on a cuppa in his rural retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris is a typical Russian name; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian holiday cottage in the countryside, so a Russian such as Boris would have one.

clue.text: Artist capturing male bird that can't fly

indicators.note: capturing means holding something within, so the artist's letters enclose the male

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A painter catches a grounded cock bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Take another look at donkeys put in reserve

indicators.note: put in says the donkeys go inside the abbreviation for reserve

parts.note: asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders the donkeys kept back in a holding pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate again, which means taking a second look at something.

clue.text: Loss of confidence resulting from former charge in court

indicators.note: in says the words for former and charge sit within the abbreviation for court

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A defendant loses nerve after an earlier accusation is heard in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' and 'court' point to a trial, but charge is a fee here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold feet is the idiom for nervousness or a loss of nerve before a big commitment.

clue.text: Fixed allowance of one sailor back working

indicators.note: back means the pair for one and sailor runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
tar is an old word for a sailor
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A single seaman is back on duty and on fixed pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I + TAR round to RATI.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed amount of food or goods allowed to each person.

clue.text: Suitable for salesperson after retirement

indicators.note: after says the turned salesperson comes behind the word for for

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Something fitting for a sales rep once they have stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means appropriate or correct, so a fitting or suitable thing is proper.

clue.text: Model in quiet Spanish region

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet
Aragon is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A fashion model lives in a peaceful corner of Spain.

clue.text: Yearly, see a nun swimming in a lake

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of a nun moving freely into another order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: Every year you can watch a nun take a dip in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual means happening once a year, which is what yearly means.

clue.text: Understudy with good reputation

parts.note: an understudy is a stand-in for an actor

explanation.surface: An understudy who is well thought of in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's standing is their status or reputation in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Champion boxer with a second assumed name

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was world heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A title-holding fighter and his corner man go by a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' suggests a boxer's cornerman, but here is only S.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false identity a person adopts, an assumed name.

clue.text: Opera song from Farrar I adored

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in Farrar I adored

explanation.surface: A fan names the operatic number by a singer they idolised.
explanation.walkthrough: Geraldine Farrar was an American soprano, which makes the surface sound like a real fan's tribute.

clue.text: Passenger vehicle coming from market overturned

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a rail vehicle running on street tracks that carries passengers.

clue.text: Sound of hooter across island

indicators.note: across means the word for hooter spans the island letter, holding it inside

parts.note: hooter is British slang for a nose

clue.text: Decent type of piano

definitions.meaning: a piano with vertical strings, as opposed to a grand

explanation.surface: Two definitions: a moral quality and an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright describes an honourable person and also names a compact vertical-framed piano.

clue.text: Short letter sent out about end of prom sinking

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the final letter of prom
out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged
short means the word letter loses its final character
end of picks the last letter of the word prom

explanation.surface: A brief note posted after the school dance's finale is going down badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts LETTER to LETTE; 'out' mixes LETTE + SENT, which goes 'about' M from prom.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlement is the gradual subsidence of a building or ground, a slow sinking.
